title: Hudspeth County School Districts: Which ethnicity was most represented in 2023-24 school year?
text:
Texas State Board Of Education Secretary Pat Hardy (2024) | twitter.com/pathardy
Texas State Board Of Education Secretary Pat Hardy (2024) | twitter.com/pathardy
Texas Education Agency.
Of the 559 students attending Hudspeth County schools, 91.2% were Hispanic. White students comprised the second-largest ethnic group in the county, making up 6.8% of the student body.
In the previous school year, Hispanic students were also the most represented group in Hudspeth County school districts, comprising 87.2% of the student body.
Ft. Hancock ISD had the most diverse student body in the county, including white, American Indian, Black, Asian, Hispanic, Pacific Islander, and multiracial students.
In the 2023-24 school year, the total number of students enrolled in the county increased 0.9% compared to the previous year.
The main offices of all districts mentioned in the story are located in cities associated with Hudspeth County.
Texas is found to be one of the least educated states in the U.S. A study from WalletHub ranked Texas 41st out of 50 states in terms of the quality of the educational system and how successful students were.
More than 5.4 million students are enrolled in public schools across Texas. Nearly one million of them live in rural areas where options for local public schools are few and far between.
The Texas education system is currently torn between public schools and taxpayer-funded private schools.
Critics argue that private schools use funds that should go to the public school system, while private school advocates claim they’re offering better education for more Texas students.
District | Most prevalent ethnic group | Percent of Total Student Body | Total enrollment |
---|---|---|---|
Dell City ISD | Hispanic | 70.8% | 72 |
Ft. Hancock ISD | Hispanic | 96.9% | 388 |
Sierra Blanca ISD | Hispanic | 83.8% | 99 |
